chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who had a slave-woman and entered into a mukātabah contract with her. The slave-woman said, “Whatever I pay from my mukātabah, I become free thereby in proportion to that.” So he said to her, “Yes.”

Then she paid part of her mukātabah, and her master had intercourse with her after that. He said: “If he compelled her to that, he is to be given the hadd punishment in proportion to what she had paid him from her mukātabah, and the hadd is averted from him in proportion to what remained due to him from her mukātabah. But if she complied with him, then she was his شریکة in the hadd, and she is to be struck with the like of what he is struck with.”

key_terms.أَمَةٌ: a slave-woman owned by a master
key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: free, meaning emancipated in proportion to payment
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِي: my emancipation contract by staged payment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master has intercourse with a partially emancipated mukātabah slave-woman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a mukātabah slave-woman who had partially paid for her freedom and was then approached sexually by her master. The ruling ties legal liability to the proportion of freedom she had acquired, and distinguishes between coercion and consent in assigning the hadd punishment.
